1	# Nxeon SEO blog batch — shared spec (read fully before writing)
2	
3	Goal: genuinely useful, keyword-targeted guides that rank and convert — NOT thin filler.
4	Google penalizes scaled thin content; every post must earn its place by being actually helpful.
5	
6	## How to write posts
7	- Create `scripts/seo-<cluster>.mjs` that `import { upsertPost, db, slugify } from "./blog-seed-lib.mjs";`
8	- Build an array of post objects, `for` loop calling `await upsertPost(post)`, then `await db.$disconnect()`.
9	- Run it with `node scripts/seo-<cluster>.mjs` from /opt/nxeon. upsertPost is idempotent (upsert by slug) and tags every post `seobatch`, and sets published=true.
10	
11	## Each post object
12	`{ title, excerpt, body, category, tags, coverEmoji, seoTitle, seoDescription }`
13	- **title**: specific, keyword-first, matches real search intent (e.g. "How to Set Up a Palworld Dedicated Server on a VPS"). Title Case.
14	- **excerpt**: 1–2 sentences, who it's for + the payoff.
15	- **seoTitle**: ≤ 60 chars, primary keyword near the front.
16	- **seoDescription**: ≤ 155 chars, compelling, includes the keyword, invites a click.
17	- **tags**: 4–6 lowercase tags.
18	- **coverEmoji**: one relevant emoji.
19	- **category**: pick a sensible one (Gaming, VPS, Security, Domains, Hosting, Tutorials, Comparisons, Networking, Control Panels, Guides, Email).
20	- **body**: markdown, **1,000–1,600 words of real value.** Do NOT set coverImage — images are backfilled later.
21	
22	## Body structure (vary it — do not stamp every post identically)
23	1. Short intro (2–3 sentences): who this is for + what they'll have by the end. No "In today's world" fluff.
24	2. Several `##` sections with real substance. Where technical, include **real, correct shell commands** in ``` fenced blocks (e.g. apt install, ufw, systemctl, java -Xmx flags, docker run). Get commands right.
25	3. Use lists for steps/specs. The markdown renderer has NO tables — present specs as bold-label bullets (e.g. `- **RAM:** 4 GB for ~10 players`).
26	4. Put `{{SCREENSHOT}}` on its OWN line at 1–2 natural spots where a system screenshot illustrates the point (e.g. after showing the control panel step). The backfill swaps these for real Nxeon UI images. Use 1–2 per post, never zero, never more than 2.
27	5. End with a `## FAQ` containing 3–4 `###` questions + short answers (targets Google featured snippets). Use real questions people search.
28	6. Final 1–2 sentence CTA paragraph linking to the most relevant Nxeon page (see LINK TARGETS).
29	
30	## Internal linking (important for SEO)
31	Every post links to **3–5** other pages, woven naturally into the prose as `[anchor text](/path)`:
32	- 2–3 links to sibling/related BLOG posts. Link to posts in your own cluster by computing their slug with the SAME `slugify` (imported) from their exact title, or to an existing post from `existing-slugs.tsv`.
33	- 1–2 links to a relevant MONEY landing page from LINK TARGETS (this is how blog traffic converts).
34	Anchor text must be descriptive (not "click here").
35	
36	## Honesty rules (non-negotiable)
37	- No fabricated benchmarks, review scores, uptime %, or customer counts. If you cite specs, keep them general and defensible ("a 4 GB plan comfortably runs ~10 players").
38	- Nxeon mentions must be truthful and light — it's a real VPS/game-server host; don't invent features. Safe truthful claims: NVMe VPS, one-click OS/app images, game-server support, free migration help, full root access.
39	- Write in a clear, confident, friendly expert voice. British/American spelling either is fine, be consistent within a post.
40	
41	## Anti-duplication
42	- Read `/tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/existing-slugs.tsv` and do NOT reuse an existing title/slug. Stay strictly inside YOUR assigned cluster so you don't collide with sibling agents.
43	- Within your batch, no duplicate slugs.
44	
45	## Report back
46	Total posts inserted, the category breakdown, and 6–8 sample `/blog/<slug>` URLs. Confirm `node` ran clean.

Writing the script... I need to handle the conflict between template literal backticks and markdown code fences in the content — I'll use double-quoted strings with escaped newlines instead, which is more verbose but avoids the syntax collision. Escaping backticks in template literals is error-prone across many code blocks, and inline code like `apt install` also needs escaping. I'm weighing whether to use separate .md files or find a cleaner way to construct the bodies without relying on backtick escaping in the template literal itself. I could use a placeholder character to avoid typing backticks in the source code, then replace it when writing the file, but that still requires managing the conceptual mapping. The safest approach is probably to bite the bullet and systematically escape every backtick as `\`` in template literals — it's tedious for 26 posts but more reliable than risking a single unescaped backtick breaking everything.

Actually, wait — I just realized backticks are perfectly fine as literal characters inside regular single or double-quoted strings, no escaping needed. The problem is that my content has lots of quotes and apostrophes, so whichever quote style I choose for the string wrapper will need escaping throughout the body text, which is just as messy.

Template literals have their own issue: backticks and `${}` syntax would get interpreted as JavaScript interpolation, which is dangerous when the content includes shell code with variables like `${HOME}` or `${STEAMCMD}`.

The cleanest approach is to store each post body in a separate file and have the script read them in, rather than trying to embed everything as strings in the code itself. $VAR syntax without braces works fine for most shell variables, so I can avoid the brace syntax that requires escaping. The real challenge is all those backticks in code blocks — I could define a constant for the fence delimiter to sidestep escaping them entirely, which would be cleaner than manually escaping each one.

Actually, the most robust approach is to write each post body into its own markdown file using the Write tool, which doesn't require any escaping at all, then have the script read them with fs.readFileSync. It's a bit more files to manage, but it completely eliminates the escaping problem and keeps the data separate from the code. I'll use a sentinel pattern like "@@@POST slug@@@" to delimit each post's body in a single markdown file, then parse it in the script. The metadata (title, excerpt, category, tags, etc.) goes in the mjs file as an array, and the script reads the corresponding body content from the markdown file by slug. Since I'm writing 26 posts at 1000-1600 words each, that's a substantial amount of content to generate, but I'll write them efficiently and genuinely.

I'll structure each post consistently—intro, prerequisites, steamcmd install, server setup, config, systemd service, firewall rules, connection steps, FAQ, and CTA—but vary the order and emphasis across posts to keep them distinct.
